neuron.title: Neuron anatomy
neuron.source: Chapter 12 lecture 1, PDF p. 2, Figure 12–2b; textbook p. 393.

parts.name: Dendrites
parts.text: Branched receptive processes. The supplied chapter describes graded input on dendrites and the cell body.

parts.name: Cell body (soma)
parts.text: The soma supports the cell and contains the nucleus. Perikaryon refers to the cytoplasm around the nucleus.

parts.name: Nucleus
parts.text: The large round structure inside the soma contains genetic material. It is not the whole cell body.

parts.name: Axon hillock
parts.text: The tapered region where the axon arises from the cell body; distinguish it from the initial segment just beyond it.

parts.name: Initial segment
parts.text: The beginning of the axon next to the hillock; the course emphasizes action-potential initiation near this region.

parts.name: Axon
parts.text: The long process carries propagated action potentials toward its terminals.

parts.name: Axon collateral
parts.text: A side branch along the axon allows one neuron to contact additional targets.

parts.name: Telodendria
parts.text: Fine terminal branches of the axon. Distinguish the branches from the knobs at their ends.

parts.name: Axon terminal
parts.text: The expanded end of a branch communicates at a synapse. Chemical terminals release neurotransmitter.

parts.name: Postsynaptic cell
parts.text: The purple receiving cell is separate from the blue presynaptic neuron.

myelin.title: Myelinated axon
myelin.source: Textbook p. 415, Figure 12–14b (axon illustration); Chapter 12 lecture 3, PDF p. 1.

parts.name: Myelin sheath
parts.text: The insulating wrapping around an axon. In saltatory propagation, action potentials are regenerated at the exposed nodes.

parts.name: Node of Ranvier
parts.text: An exposed gap between neighboring myelinated internodes.

parts.name: Initial segment
parts.text: The unmyelinated initial region before the first myelin segment.

parts.name: Cell body (soma)
parts.text: The soma contains the nucleus and supports the neuron’s metabolic activity.

spinal.title: Spinal cord overview
spinal.source: Textbook p. 436, Figure 13–2a; Chapter 13 lecture 1, PDF pp. 1–3.

parts.name: Cervical enlargement
parts.text: The upper enlargement supplies the upper-limb region through associated spinal nerves.

parts.name: Lumbosacral enlargement
parts.text: The lower enlargement gives rise to nerves associated with the lower limbs. The course also uses “lumbar enlargement.”

parts.name: Conus medullaris
parts.text: The tapered inferior end of the spinal cord proper; in the adult it is near vertebral levels L1–L2.

parts.name: Cauda equina
parts.text: The bundle of descending nerve roots below the conus, not a continuation of solid spinal cord.

parts.name: Filum terminale
parts.text: The slender supporting extension descending from the conus toward the coccygeal attachment.

section.title: Spinal cord cross-section
section.source: Textbook p. 441, Figure 13–5a; Chapter 13 lecture 1, PDF pp. 4–5.

parts.name: Posterior gray horn
parts.text: Posterior projections of gray matter contain sensory processing nuclei in the course diagram. Posterior is at the top.

parts.name: Lateral gray horn
parts.text: The lateral projection of gray matter contains visceral motor nuclei at the levels illustrated in the source.

parts.name: Anterior gray horn
parts.text: The broad anterior gray horn contains somatic motor neuron cell bodies.

parts.name: Central canal
parts.text: The small central opening contains cerebrospinal fluid.

parts.name: Posterior white column
parts.text: White matter between the posterior horns and the posterior median sulcus.

parts.name: Lateral white column
parts.text: White matter lateral to the gray horns, containing longitudinal axon tracts.

parts.name: Anterior white column
parts.text: White matter anterior to the gray horns, alongside the anterior median fissure.

parts.name: Posterior median sulcus
parts.text: The shallow posterior midline groove. Posterior is the upper edge in this source figure.

parts.name: Anterior median fissure
parts.text: The deeper anterior midline cleft, shown at the bottom of the figure.

parts.name: Posterior (dorsal) root
parts.text: Sensory fibers travel toward the spinal cord through the posterior root.

parts.name: Dorsal root ganglion
parts.text: The swelling on the sensory root contains sensory neuron cell bodies in the PNS.

parts.name: Anterior (ventral) root
parts.text: Motor axons leave the cord through the ventral root. This root has no dorsal-root-type sensory ganglion.

histology.title: Cord histology
histology.source: Textbook p. 441, Figure 13–5b: transverse spinal-cord micrograph. Posterior is at the top.

parts.name: Gray matter
parts.text: The darker butterfly-shaped central tissue includes gray horns and neuronal cell bodies.

parts.name: White matter
parts.text: The paler outer tissue surrounds the central gray matter and contains many axons.

parts.name: Central canal
parts.text: The tiny opening near the center of the gray commissure.

parts.name: Anterior median fissure
parts.text: The deep cleft on the anterior, lower side of this section.

synapse.title: Chemical synapse
synapse.source: Chapter 12 lecture 3, PDF p. 1, Figure 12–15; textbook p. 417.

parts.name: Synaptic vesicles
parts.text: Small round vesicles store neurotransmitter inside the presynaptic terminal.

parts.name: Mitochondrion
parts.text: The elongated organelle with folded inner membranes supports the terminal’s energy needs.

parts.name: Synaptic cleft
parts.text: The narrow gap separating the presynaptic and postsynaptic membranes.

parts.name: Presynaptic axon terminal
parts.text: The expanded ending of the sending neuron contains vesicles and releases neurotransmitter.

specimen.title: Dissected spinal cord
specimen.source: Chapter 13 lecture 1, PDF p. 4, Figure 13–4; textbook p. 439: anterior view of a dissected cervical spinal cord.
